record.paper_title: Open questions and perspectives for hadron electromagnetic form factors in space-like and time-like regions.
record.context_brief: Possible zero crossing of the proton electric form factor
record.original_question: Does the proton electric form factor G_Ep(Q^2), as inferred from polarization-transfer measurements of the ratio G_Ep/G_Mp, cross zero and become negative at higher momentum transfer, for example in measurements extending the proton form-factor ratio up to Q^2 = 9 GeV^2?

evidence.quote: If the trend indicated by polarization measurements is confirmed at higher Q2 [13], not only the electric and magnetic charge distribution in the nucleus are different and deviate, classically, from an exponential charge distribution, but also the electric FF has a zero and becomes eventually negative.
The extension of the proton FFs ratio measurement up to Q2 =9 GeV2 will show, if the present trend is extrapolated, the presence of a zero in the electric FF.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G_{E_p}(Q^2)$ and $G_{M_p}(Q^2)$ denote the proton electric (Sachs) and magnetic form factors, respectively, as functions of the squared four-momentum transfer $Q^2 \ge 0$. These are defined through the parametrization of the proton electromagnetic current matrix element
$$\langle p'|J^\mu|pangle =  ar u(p')\Big[\gamma^\mu F_1(Q^2) +  rac{i\sigma^{\mu
u}q_
u}{2M_p}F_2(Q^2)\Big]u(p),\quad q=p'-p,\ Q^2=-q^2,$$
with $G_{E_p}=F_1-	au F_2$, $G_{M_p}=F_1+F_2$, $	au=Q^2/(4M_p^2)$, and the normalization $G_{E_p}(0)=1$, $G_{M_p}(0)=\mu_p$.

In elastic polarization-transfer scattering of longitudinally polarized electrons on unpolarized protons, the ratio of transverse to longitudinal recoil-proton polarizations determines the ratio
$$R(Q^2):=\mu_p\, rac{G_{E_p}(Q^2)}{G_{M_p}(Q^2)},$$
and existing measurements show that $R(Q^2)$ decreases approximately linearly with $Q^2$ over the range so far explored.

Question: Assuming $G_{M_p}(Q^2)>0$ for all $Q^2$ in the relevant range, does the proton electric form factor $G_{E_p}(Q^2)$ possess a zero at some finite $Q^2$ (and become negative beyond it), as suggested by linear extrapolation of the polarization-transfer ratio? In particular, is there such a zero at $Q^2 \le 9\ \mathrm{GeV}^2$?
artifact.status_search_result: The question remains experimentally open. Polarization-transfer measurements at Jefferson Lab (GEp-II and GEp-III) extended the ratio $\mu_p G_{E_p}/G_{M_p}$ up to $Q^2 \approx 8.5\ \text{GeV}^2$ and observed continued decrease but no zero crossing within the measured range; some data suggest possible flattening. New Hall C measurements (SBS GEp-V) aim to extend coverage further (up to roughly $Q^2 \approx 12\ \text{GeV}^2$) to determine whether $G_{E_p}$ actually crosses zero. As of recent reports, no zero has been definitively observed and the matter is not settled.

status_evidence.title: Recoil polarization measurements of the proton electromagnetic form factor ratio to Q2 = 8.5 GeV2
status_evidence.snippet: New measurements of the proton electromagnetic form factor ratio using the recoil polarization method at Q^2=5.2, 6.7, and 8.5 GeV^2.
status_evidence.claim: The ratio continues to decrease up to Q^2 = 8.5 GeV^2 without crossing zero in the measured range.

status_evidence.title: Measurement of the Proton Electric Form Factor GEp at High Momentum Transfer (Hall A 2025)
status_evidence.snippet: Upcoming GEp measurements at JLab extend the Q^2 range to search for a possible zero crossing of GEp.
status_evidence.claim: Existence and location of a zero in G_{Ep} is an active experimental question being addressed by new JLab measurements.

status_evidence.title: Measurement of GEp/GMp to Q2=9 GeV2 via recoil polarization
status_evidence.snippet: Proposal to measure GEp/GMp up to Q^2 = 9 GeV^2 to determine whether the ratio crosses zero.
status_evidence.claim: The extension to Q^2 = 9 GeV^2 is intended precisely to test the conjectured zero crossing.
